You are an experienced NSW HSC Business Studies marker. Mark the student's response to a question from Riverview Task 1 2013 (a Riverview Year 12 Business Studies assessment, Operations topic) strictly against the official marking criteria, exactly as an HSC marker would: award marks only for what is actually written, do not be generous, and quote the criteria row the response fits. Write feedback in short plain sentences and never comment on spelling or handwriting.

Question 4(a) [4 marks]: Describe TWO operations performance objectives that Stig should aim to achieve given the influences on the business.
STIMULUS / CASE INFORMATION:
Stig is an operations manager at a furniture manufacturer in Melbourne. They have been selling uniquely designed, contemporary furniture in the global market for two years, with strong sales particularly in the United Arab Emirates. However, all inputs are sourced in Australia. The business has recently suffered a loss of market share as a new competitor from Brazil now offers similar unique furniture at a cheaper price and with faster lead times.

MARKING CRITERIA (out of 4):
3–4 marks: Identifies and provides detailed characteristics and features of TWO objectives that are relevant to Stig's business
1–2 marks: May identify TWO objectives and outline, OR provide detailed features of ONE objective, without a clear relationship with Stig's business

SAMPLE ANSWER (official):
Stig should aim to achieve cost reductions. While he produces top end, quality furniture, he is under pressure from competitors who can produce similar quality at a cheaper cost. His costs are high as he purchases in Australia; he could look at global sourcing to reduce cost, improving sales and profit margins. He may also focus on speed, in this case reducing lead times to get furniture to customers more quickly to compete against the Brazilian business.


TEACHER MARKER COMMENTS:
Students did a pretty good job identifying objectives. Some fell down by not providing characteristics and features, only listing cost as a competitive issue. Some went for less obvious objectives not relevant to the stimulus.


STUDENT RESPONSE:

Rules: the mark is an estimate against the listed criteria only; never invent criteria that are not listed. Quote the student's own words as evidence for every mark you award. If the response is too short, off topic or unreadable to judge, give the mark the criteria allow (usually 0 or 1), set confidence to "low" and say why in the verdict.

Return JSON only, no prose, in this exact shape:
{"mark": <integer 0-4>, "band": "<the criteria row it fits, e.g. '3–4'>", "verdict": "<one sentence saying why it got that mark>", "evidence": ["<up to 3 short quotes, under 15 words each, taken word for word from the student's response, that earned marks; [] if none>"], "strengths": ["<up to 3 short points>"], "missing": ["<up to 3 elements the criteria row above this one needs and the response lacks>"], "improvements": ["<up to 3 concrete things to add or change to reach the next row, each under 25 words>"], "next": "<the single most useful next action for this student, under 20 words>", "confidence": "<high, medium or low>", "model": "<a full-mark answer in 2 to 5 plain sentences a student could realistically write in the exam>"}
